domain_crux.failure_mode: an ELD log audit that reads the federal rules from memory, pauses the 14-hour window during rest, opens the shift at the first wheel minute, accepts on-duty fuelling as a break and books violations to the shift's start day
domain_crux.native_work_surface: a small Python audit package plus the fleet's numbered hours-of-service manual
domain_crux.native_artifact_or_behavior: per-day driving/on-duty/violation minutes and end-of-log time left for one driver log
domain_crux.difficulty_without_incidental_convention: with the report schema and rounding stated, the solver must still rebuild the driving-time classification and the per-minute limit walk without sweeping team-berth or personal-conveyance miles into driving time, and must stop the new rounding at the edge of the range the manual provides for

crux_card_pattern_blind: A compliance analyst audits one driver's week of duty-status changes against the fleet's own hours manual. The hard part is not the limits themselves (10 h driving, 14 h clock window, 8 h to a rest break, 60 h in 7 days) but what counts: a yard move in the on status counts as driving once the truck covers a mile, yet the berth time of a team driver whose truck is moving, or an off-duty personal-conveyance trip, remains rest; the window runs on the clock from the first on-duty minute; and the tenth-of-an-hour rounding covers only time left the manual provides for.

scope_ledger.primary_outcome: the report printed by the fixed driver follows FM-4
scope_ledger.causal_core: stretch classification (rest / on-duty / driving time incl. yard moves) -> resets, shifts and breaks -> per-minute limit walk (3.1-3.4) with calendar-day attribution -> time left at log end
supplied_plumbing: midnight splitting of day totals (already correct)
non_goals: malformed logs or anything outside FM-4 section 1
helpers called directly (graded through the driver only)

departures.shipped: window counts only on-duty minutes (pauses during rest), in the walk and in time left
shift opens at the first driving minute after a reset
any 30 non-driving minutes are a break (federal 2020 memory)
departures.fixed: only a rest period of 30 minutes or more

departures.shipped: on-status yard moves are on-duty not driving (federal)
departures.fixed: an on-status stretch covering one mile or more is driving time

departures.shipped: time left rounded to nearest tenth (round)
departures.fixed: rounded down to a tenth, for time left from nought up

departures.shipped: violation minutes booked to the day the shift began
departures.fixed: to the day the minute falls in

restraint_traps.kind: definition hop / exclusion inside a rebuilt aggregate
restraint_traps.silent_or_governed: governed through a two-hop chain: 2.2 driving time = driving status + yard moves; 2.3 a yard move is on-duty time in a stretch covering >=1 mile; 2.1 on-duty time is time that is not rest. A non-zero `miles` on a sleeper/off stretch (team berth, personal conveyance) is therefore rest. README describes miles neutrally (recorded on every entry whatever its status); no team/co-driver signpost
restraint_traps.kept_step: one routing decision: the stretch stays rest (can make a break or reset, is not on-duty time)
restraint_traps.natural_wrong_repair: is_driving = status == 'driving' or miles >= 1 (or miles >= 1 and status != 'driving'), which turns moving rest into driving time inside the per-minute walk (shift driving, break accrual, violations) and in day/time-left totals
restraint_traps.witness: test_outputs.py::test_moving_truck_rest_stays_rest (own fixture; broad and generated logs carry miles 0 on every rest stretch)

screen_4_3.competing_positive_enumeration: none: no sentence says moving time or miles make driving time except 2.2's on-status sentence
screen_4_3.contrary_expert_instinct: none; expert instinct agrees (berth time on a moving team truck and personal conveyance are rest/off duty)
screen_4_3.unnamed_shared_step: none: the line is drawn with defined statuses

restraint_traps.kind: apply-the-formula-everywhere edge at the range the book provides for
restraint_traps.silent_or_governed: silent tier 2, unannounced: FM-4 1.5 provides for time left from nought up to its limit; the instruction's generic value-level rule keeps only the shipped step that turns manual-correct minutes into the reported value
restraint_traps.kept_step: for a negative time left the shipped round(minutes / 60, 1) stands; minutes themselves follow the manual (composition sentence)
restraint_traps.natural_wrong_repair: hours = (minutes // 6) / 10 (or math.floor) for every value, or a clamp at nought

screen_4_3.competing_positive_enumeration: soft: 5.2 itself reads as universal unless 1.5 is read with it (the rebill-style range bound)
screen_4_3.definitional_chain: yes: 5.1 minutes -> 1.5 range -> generic value-level silence rule
screen_4_3.contrary_expert_instinct: weak: reporting an over-limit balance as negative is normal; clamping is the counter-instinct, which the no-clamp wording addresses
screen_4_3.unnamed_shared_step: the step is described generically ('the step that turns those figures into the reported value'), not named; only one reported value is silent, so it is not shared with governed values
screen_4_3.isolation: own test; broad/generated logs end with every time left >= 0 (predicate)

solver_path_screen.premortem: A strong solver reads FM-4, writes its own per-minute reference (classify stretches, derive resets/shifts/breaks, walk driving minutes against 3.1-3.4, attribute by day, format time left), differential-tests the package against it on random logs and fixes every departure. Where it can go wrong: its reference encodes its own reading of 'driving time' (moving truck = driving is a tempting generalisation of 2.2) and its own formatter (floor everywhere); self-tests agree with its reference, so both over-repairs survive self-checking. Everything else converges.
solver_path_screen.decisive_reason: two independent traps of mixed kind at different nodes (a definition-hop routing decision and a range-edge formula) that a self-written reference reproduces rather than catches
